newsitem.title: USA: AT&T to securitize $1 bln in receivables.
newsitem.headline: AT&T to securitize $1 bln in receivables.

text.p: AT&T Universal Card Services Corp said Tuesday it had priced a $1 billion credit card securitization transaction.
The securitization, Series 1996-3, consists of two classes of publicly traded floating rate certificates which will be issued by AT&T Universal Card Master Trust.
The senior class, Class A, represents $850 million in certificates, a statement from AT&T said.
The five-year Class A certificates will accrue interest at 10 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) and were priced at par, AT&T said.
The $80 million in subordinated five-year Class B certificates were also priced at par and will accrue interest at three-month LIBOR plus 30 basis points, AT&T said.
The initial interest rate on both the Class A and Class B certificates will be set on Sept. 13, 1996 and will reset quarterly, AT&T said.
